text: They say the sea keeps its own accounts. Every ship it takes, every soul... it writes them down.
Captain's log. Day nine aboard the Meridian Star. The engines failed at midnight. The wind failed with them.
The compass will not settle. The charts say open water. But we are not moving... and we are not alone.
Captain, every gauge says the engines are running. But the shaft won't turn. Something is holding us.
Holding us? In open water?
Captain. Look at the sky.
Those are not our stars. The constellations are mirrored. Everything above us is backwards.
Seventeen souls aboard. One ship. And a horizon that had begun to breathe.
Contact on the horizon. No... it's not a ship. It's a wall.
A curtain of pale light, a mile high, rippling like silk. And beyond it, the sea ran backwards.
All hands, brace! Jonas, whatever you have left, give it to me!
I have nothing, Captain! The current is taking us!
Captain... my watch just stopped. All the clocks have stopped.
And the Meridian Star crossed a line that no chart will ever show. The Zone of Anomalies.
The radio is only static. The compass is spinning. Even the seawater is giving off light.
Captain! Land! There's an island!
There is no island on this chart. Not here. Not anywhere.
A black spire rose from the mist, ringed with pale fires. A lighthouse, built by something that had never seen a ship... only the drowned.
Those lights... they're moving. Captain, they're moving toward us.
Night fell without a sunset. And below the deck, the ship began to speak.
Turn back... turn back... do not sleep.
Jonas... did you hear that?
It's the pipes, kid. Just the old pipes.
Do not sleep. They are listening.
Jonas. There's someone in the wall.
And the wall answered.
My instruments are going mad. The temperature has dropped thirty degrees in this room. Something is here.
We were the Albatross. We were the Santa Maren. We were forty ships... and now we are only the walls.
Who are you? What does this place want from us?
The lamp. The lamp calls the ships. The lamp feeds the deep. Put it out... or become the wall.
Wren Hale. Little one. Your grandfather is still at the helm of the Albatross.
Grandpa...?
Captain... look at the water.
Beneath the hull, a light drifted past. Then another. Then a shape so vast that the ship was only a leaf above it.
It's bigger than the ship. It's bigger than everything.
Nobody breathe. It hasn't noticed us.
The leviathan passed beneath them for four full minutes... and still it had not ended.
But the leviathan was not alone. And the deep was not finished.
Captain! The water is moving!
Tentacles! Starboard side!
Cut the lines! Jonas, start the engines. Now!
Come on, old girl... wake up! Wake up!
The kraken wrapped the hull, and the Meridian Star groaned like a living thing.
Flares! Light the sea! It can't stand the light!
The engines are alive! But the helm only turns one way... toward the island.
The ghosts told us the truth. The lamp holds this whole Zone together. If it goes out, it all collapses.
And the monsters?
They only follow the light. Without it, they sleep.
Then we go ashore. Eli, you have the ship. Noor, Jonas, Wren... with me.
My grandfather is in that wall, Captain. I'm going.
A boat was lowered. Four small lights crossed a black and glassy sea.
The island was not rock. It was ships. Thousands of them, fused by centuries into a single wrecked coast.
Longships. Galleons. That's a steamer from nineteen twelve. They all came here.
Wren? My little Wren... you should not have come.
Grandpa...
Climb the stair. Turn the crystal toward the sea. And run, child. Don't look back.
Four hundred steps. And on every step, a hand reaching out of the wall.
Captain... this is not a lamp. It's an eye. The island is alive.
Then the light is a lure. And we are the bait.
If we turn the crystal outward, the beam will cut through the wall of the Zone.
It's stuck! Help me push!
A hundred pale hands pressed against the wheel, beside theirs.
And the lamp turned.
Run! Back to the boat! Run!
Captain! The wall is opening! There's a gap in the light!
The island shuddered. The leviathans parted. The kraken let go.
Full ahead!
Goodbye, Grandpa.
Fair winds, my girl.
Dawn broke on an ordinary sea.
Captain's log. Day ten. We are alive. But the compass still points toward the Zone... and every night, I hear the sea writing our names.
